title: The Impact of Flyby Interactions on the Rotation of Open Clusters
comment: 17 pages, 6 figures, submitted for publication in ApJ, comments welcome
summary: The Gaia astrometric mission has provided the first evidence for the bulk rotation of open clusters. While this rotation may arise from residual spin inherited from a cluster's parent molecular cloud, it is unclear whether this explanation always suffices, as angular momentum is carried away by escaping stars on the timescale of two-body relaxation. In particular, the recent observance of significant rotation ($v_{\rm rot} = 0.81 \pm 0.06$ km s$^{-1}$) in the dynamically old ($\approx 4$ Gyr) open cluster M67 motivates a study of another potential source of spin for Solar neighborhood clusters: tidal torquing from gravitational encounters with passing giant molecular clouds (GMCs). We derive an analytic estimate for the change in angular momentum of a cluster due to an impulsive interaction with a passing GMC, and verify this expectation by performing $N$-body simulations over a range of encounter parameters using REBOUND. For highly energetic encounters, significant angular momentum can be transferred, but the stars that receive the most angular momentum are ejected, leaving the cluster remnant with negligible net rotation. Even when considering a random walk of many GMC-cluster encounters, the integrated effects of these interactions cannot explain observations of dynamically old rotating open clusters. However, we find that within $\sim 5$ Myr post-encounter, some disrupted clusters could be confused as rotating clusters while their stars are still dispersing. Using the local density of GMCs, we estimate that up to $\approx 1\%$ of open clusters in the Milky Way may carry this faux-rotation signal.

title: Partial Fragmentation of Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS)
comment: To be published in the Astronomical Journal
summary: We present time-series observations of the long period comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) obtained in 2025-2026, bracketing the comet's fragmentation in early November 2025. We show that a simple radiation pressure model can explain many of the comet's properties: the rapid fading after fragmentation, the increasing mean particle size in the projected photometry aperture, and the time dependence of the surface brightness profile. Small dust particles ($\lesssim 100 μ$m) dominate the coma, with average dust velocity $\sim$ a few $\times$ 1 meter s$^{-1}$. The nucleus radius is estimated at $\sim$0.5 km and the dust properties are consistent with, but do not prove, an origin in nucleus rotational breakup, followed by being swept down the tail by radiation pressure.

title: EP241021a as An Off-nuclear Month-duration Transient in a Dwarf Starburst Galaxy
comment: 11 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: EP241021a is a peculiar fast X-ray transient exhibiting a long X-ray plateau and an optical rebrightening, both challenging the traditional jet afterglow model. Whether its nature is a stellar explosion or a tidal disruption event (TDE) remains debated. Here we present late-time HST/WFC3 and Gemini-N/GMOS observations of its host galaxy at $z=0.748$. After $\sim300$ days post-trigger, the transient emission had faded below detection, revealing a dwarf disk galaxy with an effective radius $R_e=1.7$ kpc, a stellar mass $M_\star\sim3\times10^8M_\odot$, and a high star formation rate of $\sim5\ M_\odot\ {\rm yr}^{-1}$. Combined with previous very long baseline interferometry measurements, the transient can be located in the galactic disk with a projected physical offset of $0.95\pm0.13$ kpc from the galaxy center. Host-subtracted optical light curves show that the rebrightening ceased at $\sim47$ days, followed by a sudden drop with a power-law index steeper than $-3.3$, coincident with a similar drop in the X-ray light curve. This synchronous drop in both bands is consistent with jet shut-off, and the required month-long jet activity suggests a persistently accreting compact object fed by a TDE. Among the TDE scenarios, the off-nuclear location and the starburst host galaxy slightly favor the post-supernova micro-TDE scenario in a binary system, in which a natal kick drives the newborn compact object into a tidal disruption of its companion. Nevertheless, an off-nuclear intermediate-mass black hole TDE or a stellar-mass black hole TDE induced by dynamical scattering in a dense stellar cluster cannot yet be excluded.

title: Properties of Oxygen-rich Asymptotic Giant Branch stars in the LMC and the Milky Way
comment: 31 pages, 16 figures, 5 tables; Accepted for publication in ApJS
summary: We investigate the properties of oxygen-rich asymptotic giant branch (OAGB) stars in the LMC and the Milky Way using infrared (IR) color-magnitude diagrams, two-color diagrams, spectral energy distributions (SEDs), and variability data. The observed SEDs are analyzed with radiative transfer models to constrain the properties of the central stars and their circumstellar dust shells and to estimate distances. For OAGB stars in the LMC, whose distance is well established, a set of representative OAGB models is derived by fitting theoretical SEDs to the observations. These models are subsequently applied to Galactic OAGB stars, for which Gaia DR3 parallaxes are often uncertain, to estimate distances from SED fitting. For Galactic Mira variables, distances are also determined using a period-magnitude relation calibrated with Mira stars in the LMC. We find that OAGB stars in the two galaxies exhibit broadly similar IR properties, and that the theoretical models successfully reproduce the observed IR characteristics, despite the extreme rarity of heavily obscured objects with optically thick silicate dust envelopes in the LMC. We further examine Galactic OAGB stars associated with OH, H2O, and SiO masers, including the relationship between absolute OH maser fluxes and IR colors. In addition, we investigate the IR properties of Mira-type OAGB stars and characterize their long-term variability using archival observations together with 16 years of WISE photometric data. Finally, we present a new catalog of 70,877 Galactic OAGB stars, providing a more reliable and comprehensive dataset for future studies.

title: Exploring the Limits: Neutrino Mass and Interacting Dark Sector in the DESI Era
comment: ~ 20 pages including references, 6 Figures and 4 Tables; comments are welcome!
summary: We constrain three interacting dark matter--dark energy scenarios using cosmic microwave background measurements, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, and the PantheonPlus, Union3, and DES-Dovekie Type Ia supernova compilations. We consider interacting vacuum energy and interacting dark energy with a constant equation of state in the phantom and quintessence regimes, analyzing each scenario with either a fixed total neutrino mass or a freely varying effective neutrino mass. When the positivity prior is relaxed, all three scenarios favor negative effective neutrino masses for every dataset combination. Although some combinations permit small positive masses, none of the 95\% confidence intervals reaches the minimum mass required by neutrino oscillation experiments. Allowing the effective neutrino mass to vary produces significances for a nonzero coupling reaching approximately $3σ$, but the preferred masses remain negative. These results demonstrate that the interaction and constant dark energy equations of state considered here fail to resolve the DESI neutrino-mass tension.

title: Constraining Ultralight Dark Matter in Dynamical Dark Energy Cosmologies
summary: We investigate the cosmological implications of scalar-field dark matter (SFDM) in a dynamical dark energy framework, extending previous analyses that considered SFDM within the standard $Λ$CDM cosmological model. We consistently implement the scenario at both the background and linear perturbation levels. We perform Bayesian parameter inference using Planck CMB measurements, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, and Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae to constrain the model parameter space. Our theoretical predictions show that lighter scalar-field masses produce increasingly strong scale-dependent suppression of matter fluctuations and more pronounced modifications to the CMB temperature power spectrum, whereas heavier masses progressively approach the cold dark matter limit. For the SFDM mass, we obtain a one-sided 95\% lower limit of $\log_{10}(m_φ/{\rm eV})>-24.04$ from our main joint analysis. We find that replacing the standard cold dark matter fluid with SFDM does not qualitatively alter the constraints on dynamical dark energy or the evidence for its evolution, including a phantom crossing at low redshifts.

title: Mapping the Milky Way with SDSS-V: Galactic Genesis Selection Function and Mock Catalog
comment: 22 pages, 6 Figures, submitted to MNRAS, comments welcome!
summary: Robust chemodynamic mapping of the Milky Way requires accounting for the selection function of the survey used, the probability that a given star is included in the final catalog as a function of its observable properties. We derive the empirical selection function of the SDSS-V Galactic Genesis survey, the largest Milky Way Mapper program targeting red giant stars for Galactic structure studies. Treating the Galactic Genesis sample as a subsample of its 2MASS parent catalog, we model the selection function as a function of sky position, apparent H magnitude, and G-H color using a Bayesian binomial estimator, computing both a mean and maximum a posteriori (MAP) version. The resulting selection function reflects the survey's targeting strategy and observing history, including the transition from the pencil-beam SDSS-IV footprint to the fuller sky coverage of SDSS-V and the prioritization of the Magellanic Clouds. Using this selection function with the FIRE-2 Milky Way-mass simulations, we construct mock Galactic Genesis catalogs built on existing mock Gaia DR3 catalogs, injecting realistic photometric noise and applying the selection function via a per-star Bernoulli accept-reject procedure. We demonstrate the mock catalogs' utility with an example application to azimuthal metallicity variations in the disk. Furthermore, we release a Python package allowing users to recompute the selection function for their own samples and science cases. The package, selection function and mock catalogs will be updated and made available as the survey continues, extending the tools needed to reach the full scientific potential of SDSS-V Galactic Genesis.

title: Model-independent calibration of gamma-ray bursts with Bayesian neural networks
comment: 20 pages (12 pages of main text and references, plus 8 pages of appendices), 7 figures, 17 tables
summary: Context. Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) extend cosmological distance measurements beyond the range densely sampled by Type Ia supernovae, but their standardization requires reliable calibration and uncertainty estimates. Aims. We calibrate the Amati correlation without assuming a background cosmological model, assess its stability, and examine the cosmological reach of current and future GRB Hubble diagrams. Methods. We train a Bayesian neural network on Pantheon+ supernovae, assess and recalibrate its predictive uncertainties, and calibrate the correlation for GRBs at $z \leq 1.5$ using the D'Agostini and Reichart likelihoods. We combine the GRB Hubble diagram with supernovae, Hubble-parameter measurements, and DESI baryon acoustic oscillations. Local-regression, covariance, leave-three-out, redshift-evolution, and Efron-Petrosian diagnostics test the standardization assumptions. We also analyse idealized future catalogues of 1500 standardized GRBs. Results. The diagram reaches $z \simeq 9.4$. Covariance and leave-three-out diagnostics produce small changes in the cosmological constraints. A parametric evolution coefficient is consistent with zero, whereas the truncation-corrected diagnostic indicates marginal isotropic-energy evolution that can occur along the Amati relation. Dark-energy extensions improve the phenomenological fit relative to flat $Λ$CDM: AIC favours the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder parametrization, while BIC favours constant-$w$ dark energy. Forecasts show strong conditional model-discrimination power under the adopted uncertainty model. Conclusions. GRBs provide a complementary high-redshift extension of the supernova distance ladder. Present results do not establish an evolving dark-energy equation of state. Larger homogeneous samples are promising, but realistic selection functions and calibration systematics remain essential.

title: Relating Dark Dimension Size with Dark Energy via 5D Quintessence Potential and Casimir Energy
comment: 1+35 pages, no figure
summary: We explore effective field theory (EFT) realizations of the dark dimension (DD) scenario in which the size of the DD is determined by the competition between a 5D quintessence potential and the Casimir energy. When only contributions from massless fields are considered, the Casimir energy does not have a typical energy scale, and the 4D dark energy (DE) scale is set by the height of the 5D quintessence potential. The simple 5D model we first study has an attractive feature that the size of the DD is related to the 4D vacuum energy (VE), as outlined above. However, it turns out that the 4D VE thus obtained cannot work as the 4D DE in the standard cosmological setting. One of the discrepancies between the VE and the DE manifests in the radion dependence of the effective 4D Newton's gravitational constant. This leads us to explore a 5D model in which the 4D Einstein-Hilbert (EH) action is dominantly induced by quantum effects, leaving the radion dependence of the 4D Newton's constant subdominant. This model leads to an attractive cosmological model, realizing the mechanism explained in the beginning. We also explore a 6D model with the total internal volume fixed, to make the 4D Newton's constant independent of the radion. We first study a scenario in which the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions are of the same order. In this scenario, the physical origin of the size of the DD is left to its UV completion. Next, we turn to a scenario in which there is a large hierarchy between the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions. In this scenario, the energy scale of the 5D quintessence potential turns out to be much higher than the energy scale of the 4D DE as inferred from the cosmological observations, so we need to subtract a constant term in 4D to tune the 4D DE. This prevents us from obtaining the scaling relation for the DE expected in the dSDC.

title: QED VI: Neutral hydrogen gas in supernova-driven galactic outflows
comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables; submitted to MNRAS
summary: Winds that eject mass from galactic discs regulate the growth of galaxies, and observations show that, at least within a few kpc of the disc, most of the mass flux is carried by neutral rather than ionized material. However, it has proven difficult for simulations of supernova-driven winds to reproduce this observation, leading to speculations that the bulk of the mass must be driven by radiation pressure or cosmic rays rather than supernovae. Here we report simulations of supernova-driven winds using the GPU-accelerated code QUOKKA that reach a resolution of $Δx = 1$ pc, significantly higher resolution and simulation volume than previous work. At this resolution the winds are dominated by neutral mass, with cloud sizes, masses and column densities broadly similar to those of the HI clouds in the Milky Way's nuclear wind. The neutral material is not ballistic, but is instead driven by momentum transfer associated with drag and condensation of hot gas onto the neutral phase. By contrast, when we coarsen the resolution to values comparable to those used in earlier work, the neutral outflow weakens at $Δx = 2$ pc and disappears at $Δx = 4$ pc. We argue that this difference arises partly because lower-resolution simulations do not resolve, with a few cells, the 3-6 pc thick cooling layers in which hot gas condenses onto neutral clouds.

title: Linking Detectable Tidal Features to Stellar Halo Growth: An Integrated Analysis of the Outskirts of Massive Early-type Galaxies
comment: 20 pages, 14 figures, Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Motivated by the finding that massive galaxies with tidal features (GwT) are preferentially found in low-density environments, one wonders whether this trend arises from enhanced debris survivability or from more active mass-assembly histories. If driven by the latter, structural signatures, such as more developed stellar halos, should also form through cumulative accretion. To address this, we analyze azimuthally averaged surface-brightness profiles of 436 massive early-type galaxies from the DESI Legacy Imaging Survey, comparing the median-stacked profiles of galaxies with tidal features to those without. We find that, after resampling by stellar mass and environmental density, a subtle but systematic structural divergence emerges in the galaxy outskirts ($r>5\times r_{50}$). Specifically, the GwT population in the lower-density & higher-mass regime exhibits a relative intensity excess. This suggests that more developed stellar halos have formed, likely due to longer and/or more significant accretion events. In contrast, those in the higher-density & lower-mass regime show a relative deficiency in intensity, which is reasonable to interpret as a result of structural disruption from environmental effects rather than a lack of cumulative accretion. Our findings suggest that visible tidal features$-$particularly in massive systems within quiet environments$-$do not merely reflect recent stochastic accretion events but also hint at the long-term assembly history of galaxies. This work is a depth-limited study that offers a glimpse into an integrated analysis of tidal debris and stellar halos, thereby introducing a novel pathway to unravel the complex assembly histories of galaxies.

title: Multiplicity of Massive stars in the Milky Way (M3W). II. The brightest single O stars: variability and systemic velocities
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: (ABRIDGED) M3W studies the dynamical properties of massive stars in the solar vicinity, such as their systemic velocities, which are affected by variability effects: pulsations, line infilling by wind and disks, and incomplete knowledge about the central wavelengths. We want to increase the accuracy of the O-stars systemic velocities. We establish how different wavelength regions are affected by variability, determine the thresholds for the detection of spectroscopic binarity, and obtain accurate central wavelengths including the effects of contamination, forbidden lines, and wind infilling. We analyse 41 apparently single bright O stars. We used multi-epoch HR LiLiMaRlin spectroscopy cleaned with UNWIND and stellar models computed with FASTWIND. The epoch spectra were cross-correlated to study their variability. The RVs were computed from (a) cross-correlation of H and He lines with FASTWIND models, (b) profile fitting of metallic lines, and (c) cross-correlation of the full spectrum with a template star. A comparison between the RV dispersions for different wavelength regions reveals different groups of stars in terms of variability: (a) non-SG slow rotators, (b) fast rotators, (c) SGs, and (d) Oe stars. This is a manifestation of the different role of pulsations, winds, and disks in RV variability. We determine RV dispersion thresholds for the detection of new SBs. We also use a FASTWIND grid to establish the effects of (a) the presence of He II lines close to Balmer lines, (b) the existence of forbidden components in two He I lines, and (c) wind infilling in the determination of accurate RVs. With all of that, we determined RVs for our 41 stars, checked their accuracy, and discovered significant differences with literature values. Our analysis has further revealed four SB1 systems unknown in the summer of 2025, one new SB2, two new Oe stars, and three new Onfp stars.

title: Power spectrum of longitudinal-velocity residuals in the Galactic disk from Gaia DR3 red-giant-branch stars
comment: 12 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: Non-axisymmetric structures in the Galaxy produce coherent stellar motions in the Galactic disk. These motions are usually interpreted by assuming parameterized gravitational potentials or specific perturbation models, thereby entangling direct kinematic information with model-dependent assumptions. Using Gaia DR3 astrometry, we analyze the Galactic longitudinal-velocity residuals of nearly four million red-giant-branch stars over $-4 < X_h < 4\, \mathrm{kpc}$ and $-6 < Y_h < 6\, \mathrm{kpc}$ in the heliocentric region. We construct an empirical axisymmetric baseline without introducing any dynamical model, and compute the power spectrum of the residual velocity field. The spectrum exhibits a broad peak at spatial frequency of $f \simeq 0.12 - 0.22\, \mathrm{kpc}^{-1}$, corresponding to a scale of around $5-8\, \mathrm{kpc}$. The residual amplitude is sensitive to the adopted distance scale: inverse-parallax distances $d_\varpi$ yield a peak of around $16\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$, while the Bailer-Jones geometric distances $r_{\mathrm{geo}}$ yield around $12\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$. Minimizing the low-frequency power favors a solar radial motion of $U_\odot=10.8\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$ based on $d_\varpi$ and $U_\odot=10.4\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$ based on $r_{\mathrm{geo}}$. Collectively, the resulting spectrum establishes Gaia astrometry as a direct probe of disk-wide non-axisymmetric kinematics and provides quantitative targets for future dynamical modeling and interpretation.

title: Correlations between Dynamical Dark Energy and Neutrino Parameters
summary: Recent Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), fitted jointly with Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and Type Ia Supernovae (SNe) data, favor dynamical dark energy (DDE) over the standard $Λ$CDM model. In this work, we investigate whether the mass and degeneracy of relic neutrinos are degenerate with DDE parameters and can also account for this statistical deviation from $Λ$CDM. Using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis of a joint Planck CMB temperature, DESI BAO, and Pantheon+ dataset, we show a robust parameter degeneracy between the DDE equation of state and neutrino physics. We supplement this with a semi-analytical framework that recovers the numerical correlation, showing that the tight constraint on the CMB acoustic scale drives this degeneracy. Our results highlight the clear correlation between DDE and neutrino parameters, underscoring the critical need to jointly constrain the neutrino sector and the dark sector in next-generation cosmological surveys.

title: Theoretical Pulsation Properties of RR Lyrae and Type II Cepheids in the JWST and Roman photometric systems
comment: Accepted for publication on A&A
summary: RR Lyrae (RRL) stars and Type II Cepheids (T2Cs) are key standard candles and tracers of old stellar populations. The deep, wide-field capabilities of facilities such as the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will significantly expand their utility as a Population II alternative to Classical Cepheids for distance scale calibrations. We present theoretical pulsation properties-including light-curve morphologies, amplitudes, and multi-filter relations for RRLs (Z = 0.0001 - 0.02, M = 0.51 - 0.80, Msun) and T2Cs (Z = 0.0001 - 0.01, M = 0.495 - 0.65, Msun) to enable detailed studies of Galactic and extragalactic populations. Using alreday available non-linear convective pulsation models, we converted their predicted bolometric light curves across various chemical compositions and evolutionary stages into the JWST and Roman photometric systems. From these, we derived multi-filter Period-Amplitude and Color-Color diagrams, alongside Period-Luminosity and Period-Wesenheit relations with explicit metallicity terms. RRL relations display a significantly stronger zero-point metallicity dependence than those of T2Cs, despite sharing similar slopes. Consequently, T2Cs offer a distance scale indicator that is remarkably robust against metallicity uncertainties. As a preliminary test, we applied our metal-dependent Period-Wesenheit relations to a subset of JWST-observed RRLs in the WLM galaxy, deriving a distance modulus of mu_0 = 24.85 +/- 0.03 mag (assuming the literature average metallicity). The derived distance to WLM is consistent with most literature values, though slightly shorter than determinations based on Classical Cepheids and the Tip of the Red Giant Branch. These theoretical relations pave the way for future high-precision distance determinations and asteroseismic diagnostics with JWST and Roman.

title: Spiralling into Dark Energy: Axio-Dilaton Attractors in Light of Current Data
summary: In string compactifications, dilaton-like moduli always come paired with axions, and the two fields interact through a curved field-space metric. We study the cosmology of such an axio-dilaton system, in which the dilaton rolls down an exponential potential corrected by a polynomial prefactor and couples to a massless axion through the kinetic function $W=e^{-ξφ_1/M_p}$. A dynamical systems analysis shows that the late-time attractor follows a non-geodesic trajectory in field space with equation of state $ω_φ=(λ-2ξ)/(λ+2ξ)$, so accelerated expansion is possible for steep potentials provided $ξ\ggλ$. No physical fixed point is phantom. A Bayesian analysis with DESI DR2 BAO, binned Pantheon supernovae and Planck 2018 distance priors gives $λ\gtrsim7$--$9$ and $\log_{10}ξ\gtrsim2.5$ at 95% confidence, together with a degeneracy between the two parameters. The model is slightly favoured over $Λ$CDM by current data, while the different polynomial corrections cannot yet be distinguished. This contribution is based on arXiv:2609.22539.

title: Contributions of massive stars and classical novae to Galactic 26Al
comment: 10 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Accepted by A&A
summary: The radioactive isotope 26Al is believed to be mainly produced by massive stars and ejected into the interstellar medium through their winds and supernovae. Due to its lifetime of 1.04 Myr, it traces recent nucleosynthesis and star formation. 60Fe is a similarly long-lived (lifetime 3.8 Myr) isotope, and only originating in ccSNe. Stellar evolution models in combination with Galactic Chemical Evolution (GCE) models tend to over-predict the 60Fe/26Al ratio. Population synthesis models that attempt to explain both, the 26Al mass in the Galaxy and its spatial distribution, only match the observational constraints with an enhanced star formation rate (SFR) of >5 Msun/yr. Classical novae may contribute to the 26Al production, potentially lowering the SFR inferred from massive stars and alleviating tension in the 60Fe/26Al ratio. However, previous studies suggest their contribution is negligible or < 10%. In this work we aim to determine the mass distribution of 26Al as a function of Galactocentric radius and estimate the contribution of (very) massive stars and classical novae to the 1.8 MeV signal. We are using 20 yr of INTEGRAL/SPI observations of the gamma-ray line at 1.8 MeV to test different assumptions on the radial structure of 26Al and compare the resulting mass distribution to different GCE models. For our baseline analysis, all tested source models prefer substantial nova contributions, with best-fit fractions of 77-84%. This alleviates tension in the 60Fe/26Al ratio and lowers the SFR from 26Al measurements accordingly to 1-2 Msun/yr. While it is difficult to gauge both contributions directly, next generation MeV telescopes can potentially identify individual massive stars, such as Gamma-2-Velorum.

title: On the Evolution of Circumstellar Disks Modified by the Presence of a Binary
summary: Stars form within circumstellar disks, and some binary stars develop circumbinary disks surrounding the pair. Observations suggest that disks that form around binary star systems are less common than those around single stars. One possible explanation is that binary stars may disrupt or shorten the lifespan of their surrounding disks relative to those around single stars. To investigate this, we used the DISCO hydrodynamics code to compute the lifetimes of circumstellar disks with and without a binary. Our results indicate that binary systems can reduce the lifetime of a circumbinary disk by a modest factor of two to three compared to disks around single stars. This effect is present when the binary separation is at least one-tenth of the disk radius. While our findings show that binaries can shorten circumbinary disk lifetimes, this alone might not be enough to fully account for the scarcity of these disks.

title: Catastrophe Structure and Stability of Axion Stars
comment: 10 pages, 3 figures
summary: Axion stars are self-gravitating Bose--Einstein condensates of QCD axions or axion-like particles. Their stability determines whether they can survive as dark-matter structures and what astrophysical signatures they may produce. Here we combine a non-relativistic Schrödinger--Poisson description with catastrophe theory to develop a unified picture of axion-star stability. Beginning with the Einstein--Klein--Gordon system for a periodic axion potential, we derive the effective equations of motion and conserved quantities and construct a one-parameter family of star-like solutions. A Gaussian variational ansatz reduces the problem to an analytic energy functional $E(R;N)$. Within this model, equilibria appear and disappear through Arnold $A_2$, $A_3$, and $A_4$ catastrophes as the particle number $N$ and interaction strengths vary. A repulsive sextic interaction produces two stable branches---dilute and dense axion stars---separated by an unstable branch. The same catastrophe criteria apply beyond the sextic truncation: for the full cosine and QCD-corrected potentials, the fold conditions follow from the complete variational energy and can be evaluated numerically. We also separate stability within the collective-coordinate ansatz from full radial perturbative stability and specify the range in which the non-relativistic treatment is reliable. This framework provides a compact classification of axion-star phases and identifies model-dependent critical masses associated with collapse, bosenova-like emission, and black-hole formation.
